resources.string: The layout of the short summary written for each session. Changing it writes the summary of each client\'s last session again.

Subjective: Mark reports a tense week at work. He fears that a mistake in Thursday’s presentation will cost him his job, and he has woken around 3 a.m. on most nights. He also describes an argument with his sister Laura about who looks after their parents, which still makes him angry.

Objective: Mark spoke quickly at first and slowed down as the session went on. The therapist examined the thought “I will be fired” with him, looking at the evidence for and against it. He rated his belief in it at 80 percent at the start and 40 percent at the end. A slow breathing exercise was practised together.

Assessment: In Mark’s account the worry about work, the poor sleep and the conflict with Laura feed one another. He took an active part in the exercises and said the breathing left him calmer.

Plan: Mark will fill in a thought record three times this week, practise the breathing before bed and keep a short sleep diary. The conflict with Laura is the first topic for the next session.
